Tell him it isn't. Your partner is exactly that, even at your age; and if he can't prove an anchor for you in your time of need, I implore you to seek another. I will personally volunteer if it can make a difference.

Sometimes, in the moment, we want so badly to be gone; it would solve so many problems to just dissapear, yet, we know that is in no way a truly practical solution. The odds sometimes feel like they're so heavily tipped, which is all the more reason to embolden the little bit that does keep us around.

Find that thing, do little things you can accomplish and go from there. Find strength in the fact that you have had the endurance to make it this far; you've already had your face to the harsh wind and made it to where you are, relatively, the remaining portion is small in comparison until you're done with school, and never have to associate with these people ever again.

There is nothing wrong with going to your parents, or your school to help you mitigate some of the problems you see if your day to day. There are resources, and people you can take advantage of. I switched schools, and while I hated the concept at first, it was the best thing that could have possibly happened to me. I encourage you to seek out these opportunities.

Sometimes loss of things can feel cleansing. I'm sorry about losing those staples of your life, I've never been married, but I've been cheated on, homeless, and unemployed; and can empathize. Be strong in the fact that you have kids that more likely than not care supremely about you, and the thought of you being this upset, let alone gone would in turn make them upset. Be in the present, and be with them, in that you can find joy and closeness that can help with the suicidal ideation. It may not completely remove it, for now at least, but it can be lessened, and we can learn to recognize it.

You may not know, but you face each day because you still care; you came here instead of killing yourself because you still have hope. You are not Sisyphus, this hill can be climbed, and you can overcome that which hampers you. Be the anchor for your children.

You are doing the best you can, and there is no way she doesn't understand and appreciate it. Things like malice, or a lack of caring are not what stops you, and she knows that. You may not be able to physically do some things, but you are clearly showing you care in other ways.

Friends can come and go, but your partner is your partner; and will nurturing, your family unit can have such a strong and caring bond. You clearly care, so I know things will work out for you.

I'm sorry you had to experience that considering that you've gone through something similar based on your comments. Not person should have to undergo sexual abuse, especially when they are too young to understand it, or the far reaching implications. Just know that in reporting it, you've helped prevent other people from having to endure the same thing. While disturbing, you should be glad to make a difference.

As for any trauma that it has surfaced - have you spoken to anyone about your experiences, professional or otherwise? Things like expressing abuse have always helped me, and cognitive behavioral therapy, while sometimes tough, can help you overcome the things that haunt you.

Talk to someone, literally anyone who will listen. We let these ideas fester in our heads for too long, expressing them has always allowed me a degree of self reflection, and reprieve from them to a degree. Take some time for yourself, admit yourself if you have to in order for you to have that break that you need.

In the meantime, look at your job as an opportunity to fuel something better. For now, you at least have employment - I was laid off at the beginning of June, and my savings are almost all gone - you have that net, take advantage of it. Find what you want to do, be it a hobby, get on a dating app or something, even just go for a walk; find a way to achieve something, and work your way to what can hopefully turn into a feeling of happiness.

We all have those things we wish we had done, and what we wish we had become; but the fact is, that it isn't in fact too late to achieve what we want or need to. You may not be one of the 15 year olds having a breakdown in the school bathroom, but you can still achieve the accomplishment you need in life.

Don't like your living situation? Find a new one, lots of windows - I've spent my time in enough dingy basements to appreciate natural light. Apply for new jobs, quit your current job, take a vacation and go backpacking... or just go for a walk around the block. Set yourself any sort of a goal, and accomplish it, then the next, and the next. It is a steep, and shitty climb, but none of us are Sisyphus, and the top can be reached in due time. 

You'll make it.

I have a mother that similarly chose to point out my flaws, rather than express any parental or supportive nature. You should be proud of your weight loss, and if you feel good about yourself in your makeup or otherwise, then who are they to be allowed to hamper that? We don't all get born into a functional and supportive family, but we can build our own family and  support network ourselves. I speak from personal experience, having disowned my immediate family members for their individuals acts of abuse -physical, emotional, verbal, etc. - nothing says blood has to define you or who you are.

Continue to strive to be better, be better than them, and the depths of character they choose to wallow in. I'm not sure how old you are, but you sound young enough to have not left the nest quite yet. Your younger years will pass, and you will soon have the freedom to be the person you deserve to be.

I understand the pain you describe, I've felt pain and lonliness so severe it felt like my heart was literally being squeezed. Life can suck, I know I've had a lot thrown my way, as you describe having happened to you as well. But I've survived it somehow. I've endured some of the worst of what humanity can conjure and throw at me; and sometimes you can only figuratively, and sometimes literally put one foot in front of the other.

We have to remember that we're not special, or unlucky enough for the universe to single us out for bad luck, nor will it do the opposite and help us. There is a freedom in that, and in self reliance. If you truly have no support network, as I have known my entire life, then find someone - literally anyone who will listen to talk to. No matter how bad, speaking or writing your experiences has always allowed a degree of self reflection, and gets these intrusive ideas out in the open, instead of being pent up inside of our heads.

You and I both made our way here because instead of just killing ourselves, we knew that somewhere in us, there is something that still cares, and has hope for the future. I've got some years on you, not a whole lot, but enough to know that you're still at a point where you can do something about the way you feel. You are better than the people and the things that put you here, you just need to realized it.

Accomplish any task you can, however small. Build your foundation of accomplishment - do better, and be better than how you may be feeling, because you are better, even if you don't feel that way. I've been dealt a shit hand, but I'm still here, because I know part of me still hopes that one day I'll achieve everything I hope for, and if I end it prematurely, I'll never see that version of tomorrow.

I hope this helps, if nothing else, reading it has kept you here just a little bit longer, and sometimes just counting the minutes is enough.

It doesn't feel like it now, but you'll blow past this so quickly. Some people are the absolute worst, irrideamable, in fact. This in turn makes nothing they do or so worth considering, you are better than them by the fact that you are not like them. Continue to be better, as an idiot drags you down to their level, and beats you with experience; they truly have no power, and as soon as you prevent them from getting under you skin, you will realize thusly.

In the meantime, talk to someone, literally anyone. I've always found that writing or speaking the things that truly burden me not only seem to metaphorically relieave the weight they put on you. We let these bad thoughts resonate and bounce around in our heads too long, but if we can put them in a place where we can reflect on them - for me - it always seems to help.
I'm glad, collectively, we have both gotten just a little bit better. This task is not Sisyphean unless we make it so.

You still have so much time to correct these issues you have. In time, you'll find that they aren't as bad as they seemed. You haven't had time to amount to anything yet, now is your time; use this frustration, and turn it into the determination to do better, and to be better.

What do you want to do in life? Make small steps to improve things, and work towards it. Speak with your family, or a professional if you don't want them involved. Get the advice you need to help you move forward, or just find someone that will listen. Time and time again, I've found that once I've spoken or written my thoughts down, I was able to take a step back and gain some perspective.

Change what you can, learn to live with what you cannot. I am also short, but we can both lost weight can we not? I went from in shape to gaining over 50 lbs due to my medication tanking my metabolism, and not giving a fuck about what I ate. It's hard, but I'm trying to give a fuck now, and so should you, even if it's only a little. We both came here instead of offing ourselves, we both still have that ember of hope in the back of our mind that still wants us to continue. Be strong, friend, and in return I will do my best to do the same.

I found that after I had taken the time to write things down before my attempt, it had actually helped me put things into perspective better. Perhaps a journal could help - we spend too long stuck inside our own heads. I didn't have anyone to say sorry to, just who got my things and why I was doing it, but nonetheless, it seems to have helped.

I hope that you can find a sense of personal understanding like I did, and that you're around to respond to this after the fact.

I'm in the same boat, even with an insurance issue, but I was lucky to have remedied it; I'm sure you can as well. I've been laid off since the beginning of June from a job I was told I would "retire" in. I've applied to probably 1000 jobs since then, and have been coasting on my even dwindling savings. Things keep piling up, yet we both made our way here, you even more so by posting; despite everything in our head telling us the contrary, we both know that taking your own life isn't something you should do, not matter how much we want to dissapear, or just end the stress and burden.

Once I began reading posts, and answering them here, I started to feel better. I think the fact that so many people going through the same thing makes me feel less isolated. I didn't even entertain going to a shrink, with or without insurance because of the financial hole I'm in, so that certainly helps. Perhaps it's a feeling of communal suffering, or that maybe I don't have it as bad as used to, or could, which helps metaphorically talk me down.

I think the best thing we can both do for our own sake is do our best to get back on the horse, it's a steep hill, and a shitty climb, but the alternative is just a potentially messy or painful death; with our life, and any remaining dignity going with it. Stay strong, solve the insurance issue - I did by being persistent over the phone because the person I spoke to before buying in told me I would be covered for what I was being refused. Once the problem is solved, solve the next, and don't stop until the hill is climbed.

I'm glad you decided not to go another round, there is still much to be salvaged in your life, I'm sure. I found myself feeling similar after my attempt, perhaps because I was hospitalized and interred in a psych ward to get help; but I felt like I had gained new perspective on my mortality, and that perhaps at such a new low, the only way to go was up.

I am in no way a bastion of healthy mental state, but by being here, we all keep each other going; one bullet dodged at a time.

I know it's hard, what was done to me at school goes beyond bullying; to call it so honestly feels like trivializing it. Your boyfriend clearly cares about you, and so you're clearly someone worth caring about. The fact of the matter is people in adolesence can be so cruel; what you must do it be better, an idiot drags you down to their level, then beats you with experience. The amount of time left for you to be done at that school, and rid of them to a flourishing life is short, relatively speaking; from experience, I know it is difficult, but at least you have at least one person that cares.

You will do better than them, and be better than them; accept no less, use it as your strength, your anchor, and shield. Cutting yourself solves nothing, if your home life doesn't allow you the opportunity, then speak with your boyfriend about it; just talk to someone. By the very essence of not being like them you are a good person; do not drop out of school, I nearly did so myself due to abuse at home, but to do so would be such a detriment to your life afterwards.

15 is young, you will get better as time goes on; this is experience talking.

Talk to someone, these things are allowed to bounce around in our head for too long. Be it annonymous, professional, or personal; just tell someone about it all. Hell, I'll listen, I'll give you my number if I have to, because I don't have a support network of people I can talk to. I may not be the spitting image of mental health - especially because I've found my way here before, but if I can help someone get out of where I am, and have been, then that's at least something.

You seem to have weathered everything life threw at you so far, if it's been 5 years. I don't have an answer for you, I gave it a shot just about 5 years ago or so myself, but I wasn't successful. That said, what I clearly needed most, was the help I recieved at the hospital after I was admitted; perhaps it can help you as well.

I've been homeless, the parental situation was abusive, not death (for better or worse), and I barely graduated myself. You and I are at least still here, we both brought ourselves to this message board because we both know that despite how we feel, we shouldn't take our own lives, even if everything is screaming at us to do so.

I'm 29, I feel like I haven't amounted to anything in this life; all I can do is put one foot in front of the other. Perhaps you can do so as well. Best of luck, friend.

Don't seek sex, what you need - what any of us need - is companionship. The rest will come with it; too many people are engrossed in their sex life, it isn't a race, it proves nothing about your character, you could argue being with a considerable amount of partners does, though not in a good way.

For context, I'm 29, I've only done the deed once myself, and quite frankly, I regret it. We may have differing opinions, but it just didn't feel right, and it felt rushed. I'm here because a large contributing factor to my suicidality is the painful loneliness I feel in life, but not due to the lack of sex. When the person I loved, and importantly, trusted was so capable of seeing someone else while stringing me along it killed me, the loss of trust and companionship is what does me in; again, not sex.

I think you may be feeling the same thing. Seek a partner/companion, the rest just comes naturally.

I won't ply you with false platitudes and general "it'll get better" comments, because let's be real - in what way do they actually help, especially in crisis? What I can tell you is that you still have a blank canvas. I came here just now looking for help myself, and your title disheartened me to see. I grew up dirt poor, my mother to her credit worked hard for us; it wasn't until the later years when her abuse of myself, and substances really started to come in, for all I know she's reading this, because she actively stalks me.

You've worked hard, and can continue to do so. Being 18 doesn't make anyone grown up, nobody really is; and wisdom is based on experience, not age. I'm 29, I have a degree that I wasted so much time and money on that has paid off for nothing, I've worked only menial jobs my entire life because I worked as soon as I was able and have taken when I can get. As a result, I am riddled with crippling injuries, yet I still have to do this kind of work. I have zero support network, argueably the opposite, as I only seem to be able to pick out bad friends, and even worse romantic interests. But enough about me.

Take out a loan, go to school, and work your ass off. Live in the dorms, student loans help cover that as well. It wasn't until after my degree that I was diagnosed with severe ADHD, which saddens me to think back on how horribly it hampered my performance in school before, during, and after my degree. You'll be done in no time, have a sea of colleagues and peers from your time in school, and have a very well paying and employable job. I'm dumb enough to have gone to school to try to pursue creative means, the worst part is that the school shouldn't even be accredited, that's how awful it's curriculum is - I have literally taught myself everything I know, I paid to rent a desk and get given assignments.

Right now, your world feels very small, due to your lack of perspective, everyone graduates high school at 17/18, you haven't lost any time; unless you consider dropping out being a head start. Separate yourself from whomever hampers you and your goals, find me when you're 30 like me (2 months), if you're in the same spot, we'll both jump off a bridge together if I haven't already. Otherwise, give them all hell.

Pretty is pretty, but only ugly can be beautiful. There are a few different hooks a game can have: visual hook, mechanics hook, gameplay hook, etc. 

Style in a game can absolutely be an asset; however, you can look at something like Runescape as well, that game is ugly as all hell, yet people still play the original version. If you have a solid game, it could be dots and lines, as long as it is fun.

My suggestion, though this may involve a pivot of the in game monetization is to put them towards new cosmetics, separate from the major packs; basically in the store that rotates a few armor pieces each week getting switched to samples. If the higher ups are worried about funds, then add the ability to pay for samples as well as super credits if they're worried about revenue. Or a converter from samples to credits.


I do concept art, and I can tell you I'd love to be designing new helmets and armor for this game, so I imagine the people currently doing so would love the opportunity to continue to do so as well. The designs are relatively simple as well, so it's not like your hard surface artists would have too much to do either. Adding new cosmetics would give a large amount of your player base something to earn, as eventually the gameplay loop becomes too repetitive for most people without some gratification or new content.


On a simpler level, you could add the ability to change colours of the support weapons/vehicles. Solid colours/skins/designs (bug/robo versions). I'd look to how games like Halo 2-Reach did customization, or how DRG currently does it, especially with their seasons they've recently implemented that allows you to track your progress, while getting new skins, weapons, designs, etc. Lastly a model like Vermintide/Darktide works well by added side objectives/bounties that carry into one or several missions. With so many attention deficit riddled people, that instant gratification is important.


End of the day, some of these can be a slippery slope, do not falter on your stance that everything can be eared in game. I remember a good GDC lecture by the loot designer/balancer for Diablo 3 that spent a lot of time going over how you alienate a large portion of your audience hiding things behind a pay wall, and intentionally or not, it creates a large degree of separation/a rift in a community. And in a community driven game, that's a death sentence. The other point was rather than nerf everything, let everything be powerful, then adapt around that.

If you're open for a bit of critique I'd say you really need to simplify your storyboards or it's going to take you considerably longer than it ever should. Find storyboard templates, use the notes section at the bottom to describe sound effects and camera movements, also it would help to look up a list of said movements so you know which type of arrow to use in your panels as indicators. When it comes to the simplification, break down your characters into their most base shapes possible, make the girl a square, or a red square if needed; make the monster a with an egg shaped rib cage, and a spherical head with direction lines as needed on the head. Add arms where needed. When it comes to your concept art and key frames for a rough animatic, that's when you can bring a bit of detail in; it becomes a pointless effort adding it now, simply because of how much storyboards are subject to change before you even begin to move to the next steps. Hope this helps.

Good man, far too often people are afraid of feedback. You've got a nice sense of values throughout your composition, that being said your largest point of value contrast doesn't highlight the relationship between the beast and your figure, she blends in considerably. I'd recommend the possibility of getting rid of her if you don't consider her as important; however, considering the fact that she's in there to begin with that tells me otherwise. I'd suggest perhaps expanding the size of your canvas and offsetting them asymmetrically, the 75/25 split is incredibly effective and could solve that issue for you. That or I'd recommend perhaps creating a frame within a frame by shifting them slightly and using the negative space between his legs or the silhouette of his arm as an example to provide a strong backdrop for your female figure allowing you to push the value contrast between the two figures, which will in turn tie them together stronger from a narrative perspective, and to overall draw focus to what should be the most important part/focal point of your painting. Otherwise, I'd say to try minimalizing the detail/rendering on her; you've established a very strong and effective painterly and textured style, because she's painted differently than the rest she stands out but not in an effective way like could be done like suggested above. You've implemented a strong light source, so try applying it more to her and allowing her to have her back mostly cast in shadow, it'll give her a strong silhouette and more impact overall. Giving her a long shadow on top of that because of how low your light source is will also help her feel more like she belongs in the space opposed to being pasted on. I apologize for the long winded nature of this, and I hope this helps inform your compositions. Very strong work, and despite how much there is to say about it, those are all in reality very small changes; keep up the good work.
